```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(beFAIR)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")

# All chunks run from inside the FAIRground directory
dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "beFAIR_smoke")
dir.create(dir, showWarnings = FALSE)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = dir)
```

This vignette walks through the fastest path to a working local database: connect,
create a project, initialise, run the ETL, and check that data arrived. It takes
about one minute to run on a fresh installation.

The examples below use an **in-memory SQLite database** and a **built-in dummy
FAIRground**, so no external server or DSN configuration is needed.

---

## 1. Connect to the database

```{r connect}
con <- FAIRgroundConnect(drv = RSQLite::SQLite(), dsn = ":memory:")
```

`FAIRgroundConnect()` stores the connection as the session default. Every
subsequent beFAIR function will use it automatically unless you pass a
different connection explicitly.

> **In production** you would use a DSN instead:
> `FAIRgroundConnect("MY_DSN")`. See `?FAIRgroundConnect` for ODBC options.

---

## 2. Create a FAIRground project

```{r start-project, message=FALSE}
startProject(dir = dir, dummy = TRUE)
list.files(dir)
```

`dummy = TRUE` copies a set of example studies, experiments, and analyses into
the new project directory. These include two clinical studies and several
immunology experiments — enough to demonstrate the full pipeline.

---

## 3. Initialise the database

```{r init}
databaseInitialize()
DBI::dbListTables(con)
```

`databaseInitialize()` creates the two core registry tables (`table_script` and
`table_codebook`) plus reference tables for gene symbols and glycan nomenclature.
No study data yet — that happens in the next step.

---

## 4. Run the ETL pipeline

```{r update, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
databaseUpdate()
```

`databaseUpdate()` scans the project directory for ETL scripts, runs each one,
validates the output against its codebook, and loads the results into the
database. It is the single function you call whenever scripts or data change.

---

## 5. Verify data loaded

Check which tables now exist:

```{r list-tables}
DBI::dbListTables(con)
```

Pull the participant table to confirm real rows arrived:

```{r participants}
participants <- collectTable("participant")
nrow(participants)
head(participants[, c("participant_id", "study_id", "age", "sex")])
```

You can explore any other table the same way:

```{r studyarms}
collectTable("studyarm")[, c("studyarm_id", "study_id", "studyarm_name")]
```

---
